**Finding submitted: MISSING (insurance article absent).**

- **Investigation:** Full-document search surfaced only asset-specific insurance references — replacement-value cover for consigned Products with IBM as joint insured (§13.1(b)), IBM-carried tooling insurance (§21.2), and freight/"NIC" insurance folded into price (§10.5, Attachment 1 §1.15). The Loan Agreement's Risk of Loss section (§8) shifts risk but requires no policy. No CGL, E&O, cyber/privacy, workers' compensation or certificate obligation exists anywhere, so even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) fails.
- **Target level:** Preferred, since the clause is drafted from scratch for a vendor holding our consigned inventory, occupying premises and accessing our I/T systems.
- **Redline:** One `insert_after` op adding Section 16.22 (Insurance) at the end of the GENERAL article, carrying exactly the six preferred elements. The cyber trigger is drafted to reach all data "belonging to, supplied by, or processed for IBM" rather than named examples. Per drafting discipline, I omitted the model language's at-own-expense and one-year survival tail as non-element boilerplate.
